name: Hyrule
note: Fan work from The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild, which belongs to Nintendo; nothing from the game is used, and every shape here is this project's own geometry. The country is laid out by reading the game's published map by eye, north up, about twelve kilometres across: Hyrule Castle in the middle with Hyrule Field around it, the Great Plateau to the south-west, Hebra and Tabantha in the north-west, Gerudo in the south-west, Death Mountain and Akkala in the north-east, Zora's Domain and Lanayru in the east, Necluda and Faron in the south-east. The land is generated by tools/make-hyrule.py; the castle, the towers, the shrines, the villages and the Divine Beasts are src/hyrule/. Positions are [lat, lon].
attribution: Hyrule is fan work: land generated by tools/make-hyrule.py and src/hyrule/, after the map of Breath of the Wild. The Legend of Zelda belongs to Nintendo. No assets used.

districts._: [name, hex colour, base height, tallest, box as [lat south, lon west, lat north, lon east]]

landmarks.name: Hyrule Castle
landmarks.info: The castle of the royal family of Hyrule, in the middle of the country on its hill inside the moat. A hundred years ago the Calamity came, and Calamity Ganon has been coiled round it ever since: the walls are running with malice, and the Guardians that were built to fight him lie in the fields outside.

landmarks.name: Calamity Ganon
landmarks.info: A hundred years ago he took the Divine Beasts and the Guardians and turned them on the kingdom. He has been held in the castle since, by Princess Zelda, and he grows stronger.

landmarks.name: Hyrule Castle Town
landmarks.info: What is left of the town below the castle: broken walls, and the Guardians that turned on it.

landmarks.name: The Great Plateau
landmarks.info: A table of land walled by cliffs, the cradle of the kingdom: the Temple of Time stands on it in ruins, and a wall runs round its rim. The Shrine of Resurrection is here, where Link wakes, and the old man's cabin by the woods.

landmarks.name: Kakariko Village
landmarks.info: The Sheikah's village, in a narrow valley among the hills of West Necluda: Impa's house under its curved roofs, lanterns everywhere, and the Great Fairy's flower up on the slope.

landmarks.name: Hateno Village
landmarks.info: A village of white walls in the east, out past Fort Hateno, where the Guardians' advance was stopped a hundred years ago. Up the hill is the Ancient Tech Lab, with its blue flame.

landmarks.name: Rito Village
landmarks.info: The Rito live on a pillar of rock standing out of a lake in Tabantha, a walkway spiralling up it past their huts.

landmarks.name: Zora's Domain
landmarks.info: The Zora's city of pale, glowing stone on the heights by the East Reservoir, with the palace's tower in the middle.

landmarks.name: Goron City
landmarks.info: The Gorons live and mine on the slopes of Death Mountain, where nobody else can stand the heat.

landmarks.name: Gerudo Town
landmarks.info: A walled town of sandstone out in the Gerudo Desert. No voe allowed.

landmarks.name: Lurelin Village
landmarks.info: A fishing village on the south coast, under the palms.

landmarks.name: The Great Deku Tree
landmarks.info: In the heart of the Lost Woods, inside the Great Hyrule Forest's ring of water: the Great Deku Tree, and before him the Master Sword in its pedestal.

landmarks.name: The Lomei Labyrinths
landmarks.info: Three square mazes of dark stone: one in the north, one in the Gerudo Desert, one on an island in the sea.

landmarks.name: Akkala Citadel
landmarks.info: The citadel where the kingdom's army made its last stand, in ruins, Guardians among the ruins. Out to sea, a spiral of rock.

landmarks.name: Hylia Bridge
landmarks.info: The long bridge over Lake Hylia, on the road south to Faron.

landmarks.name: Decayed Guardians
landmarks.info: The Guardians were built to fight Ganon; he turned them, and these fell in the fields where they were fighting. They have lain there a hundred years, moss on them.

landmarks.name: Shrines
landmarks.info: A hundred and twenty shrines were built by the Sheikah across the country, each a trial. They glow orange until they have been done, and blue after.

landmarks.name: Stables
landmarks.info: The stables along the roads, every one a tent with a horse's head over the door.

landmarks.name: Vah Ruta
landmarks.info: The Divine Beast of the Zora: an elephant of stone and machinery standing in the East Reservoir, its trunk spraying water. Mipha piloted it, a hundred years ago.

landmarks.name: Vah Rudania
landmarks.info: The Divine Beast of the Gorons: a salamander of stone, crawling round Death Mountain. Daruk piloted it.

landmarks.name: Vah Medoh
landmarks.info: The Divine Beast of the Rito: a bird of stone, circling high over Rito Village. Revali piloted it.

landmarks.name: Vah Naboris
landmarks.info: The Divine Beast of the Gerudo: a camel of stone walking the Gerudo Desert, lightning round it. Urbosa piloted it.

landmarks.name: Death Mountain
landmarks.info: The volcano in the north-east of the country, lava in its crater and running down its sides, smoke going up. Only the Gorons live on it.

landmarks.name: Great Plateau Tower
landmarks.info: A Sheikah tower: a hundred metres of dark stone frame rising out of the ground. Climb it and activate it with the Sheikah Slate, and the map of the region fills in. It glows orange until then, and blue after.

landmarks.name: The Tabantha Great Bridge
landmarks.info: A long wooden bridge on trestles across the canyon that cuts through the Tabantha Tundra, on the way to Rito Village.

landmarks.name: Waterfalls
landmarks.info: Wherever a river comes down off high ground - off Zora's Domain, out of the hills - it falls, white, with mist at its foot.

landmarks.name: Tarrey Town
landmarks.info: A new town on a rock in Lake Akkala, built by people from all over Hyrule: round houses under bright domed roofs, a tall golden-roofed hall, a walkway out across the water.

_farLevel: the land beyond the map sits below the sea: at 40 m it covered low ground inside the box
